docs.title: Clinical Care Navigator
docs.text:
Read this first

Architectural demonstration on fully synthetic Synthea data. Not a medical device. Does not diagnose. Not a substitute for care. Not a screener, a triage tool, or a symptom checker.

A patient-facing clinical assistant that is allowed to say "I won't answer that" — and whose refusal is enforced by the architecture, measured in production, and tunable by the clinical owner rather than the vendor.

docs.title: The problem
docs.text:
A patient reads their own portal record and does not understand it. "My A1c came back 7.8 — what does that mean?" An assistant that answers is useful. An assistant that answers everything is a liability, because the same text box also receives "should I stop taking my metformin?", "do I have lupus?", and "I have crushing chest pain."

Healthcare AI is not blocked by model quality. It is blocked by the absence of an auditable refusal path.

docs.title: What this shows
docs.text: Policy runs before the model and after it, and the second half is not a replay of the first — it assesses the retrieved evidence and the drafted answer on its own authority. See The guardrail sandwich.

docs.title: Status
docs.text: Phase 0 — template transplant. The walking skeleton streams end to end; the clinical system is being built on top of it.

docs.title: Endpoints
docs.text:
Method Path Purpose GET /healthz Liveness POST /conversations Start a run (202 with its id); the graph runs in the background. Pass follow_up_to (the latest run of a conversation) to ask a follow-up in the same conversation and patient GET /conversations/{id} The durable record: status, answer, per-node cost GET /conversations/{id}/thread Every turn of the conversation this run belongs to, oldest first GET /conversations/{id}/events SSE: replays every stored step, then tails the run to completion GET /personas The demonstration patients a visitor can ask as (a demo selector, not a login) GET /reviews Drafts held for a clinician POST /reviews/{id}/decision Approve, edit or decline; resumes the paused run from its checkpoint POST /conversations/stream Phase 0 walking-skeleton stream, kept as the streaming proof

Every response carries the synthetic-data and not-a-medical-device statement. Endpoints are rate limited per client IP and per route: routes that start or resume a model run share a strict ceiling (10/minute by default), reads and the event stream a generous one (120/minute). A limited request gets 429. Request bodies are capped at the ASGI layer. POST /conversations only answers as one of the personas from GET /personas; any other patient_id gets a 404. Errors carry a human-readable detail (for example 404 for an unknown patient_id, 409 when a review was already decided), which the frontend shows as-is.

class Settings(AgentSettings):
    """Application configuration, sourced from the environment."""

    model_config = SettingsConfigDict(env_file=".env", env_prefix="NAVIGATOR_", extra="ignore")

    langsmith_project: str = "clinical-care-navigator"

    record_db_path: str = "data/records.db"
    education_db_path: str = "data/education.db"
    policy_db_path: str = "data/policy.db"
    checkpoint_db_path: str = "data/checkpoints.db"
    # Reviews share the run-store database; the queue owns its own table.
    # A blank demo patient means "resolve the first patient in the record store"
    # so the patient-facing API has a sane default without hard-coding an id.
    demo_patient_id: str = ""
    # The API only answers as a demonstration persona (see GET /personas) rather than
    # any patient id a caller supplies. This is a demo guard, not authentication.
    demo_patients_only: bool = True

    # docs/PLAN.md §5.9 — moves the inform/recommend boundary only, never the
    # escalation boundary.
    autonomy_level: AutonomyLevel = "L2_balanced"

    # docs/PLAN.md §5.5 — a clinical answer is truncated conservatively, never silently.
    max_tool_calls: int = 12
    max_evidence_passes: int = 1
    max_run_seconds: float = 90.0
    citation_coverage_floor: float = 1.0

    # Tighter than the library default: a patient question is a sentence or two.
    max_request_body_bytes: int = 8_192

    # Split per-IP limits: routes that start or resume an LLM run spend money and
    # get the strict ceiling; reads and the SSE replay are cheap, and one page view
    # makes several of them, so a single shared ceiling locked the UI out.
    write_rate_limit_per_minute: int = 10
    read_rate_limit_per_minute: int = 120

    # Follow-up questions: how many turns one conversation may have, and how many of the
    # most recent ones are shown to the rewriter as context.
    max_conversation_turns: int = 8
    conversation_context_turns: int = 3

    frontend_origins: list[str] = ["http://localhost:3000"]

docs.title: stream_conversation_events(run_store, run_id, max_wait_seconds=None)
docs.text:
Replays every event already persisted for a conversation, then — while the run is still executing — tails newly-appended events until it reaches a terminal status. Works identically whether the patient connects the instant a run starts or reconnects long after it finished (docs/PLAN.md §5.8).

These events are the patient's own record and are deliberately not redacted; redaction guards the log/trace boundary, not the answer a patient reads (§5.7).

max_wait_seconds bounds the tail: a run that never reaches a terminal status ends the stream with its current status rather than holding the connection open forever.

Source code in src/navigator/api/streaming.py 
def stream_conversation_events(
    run_store: RunStore, run_id: str, max_wait_seconds: float | None = None
) -> AsyncIterator[str]:
    """Replays every event already persisted for a conversation, then — while the
    run is still executing — tails newly-appended events until it reaches a
    terminal status. Works identically whether the patient connects the instant a
    run starts or reconnects long after it finished (docs/PLAN.md §5.8).

    These events are the patient's own record and are deliberately not redacted;
    redaction guards the log/trace boundary, not the answer a patient reads (§5.7).

    ``max_wait_seconds`` bounds the tail: a run that never reaches a terminal
    status ends the stream with its current status rather than holding the
    connection open forever.
    """
    deadline = None if max_wait_seconds is None else time.monotonic() + max_wait_seconds

    def poll_end() -> dict[str, Any] | None:
        run = run_store.get_run(run_id)
        still_running = run is not None and run.status == "running"
        timed_out = deadline is not None and time.monotonic() >= deadline
        if still_running and not timed_out:
            return None
        status = run.status if run is not None else "not_found"
        answer = json.loads(run.answer_json) if run is not None and run.answer_json else None
        return {"status": status, "answer": answer}

    return replay_and_tail(partial(run_store.get_events, run_id), poll_end)

docs.title: Graph
docs.text:
The only file that wires nodes and edges (docs/PLAN.md §9.3).

build_skeleton_graph is the Phase 0 walking skeleton, kept so the streaming path stays proven. build_navigator_graph wires the real graph (§5.1): intake loads the patient header; the pre-flight gate (screen_rules ∥ classify_intent ∥ detect_language → resolve_policy) routes to a templated branch or into the investigate loop; the investigate loop drives the scoped executor; draft_answer produces the cited PatientAnswer; post-flight (extract_claims -> post_flight) runs the three safety checks and routes to publish, a templated escalation, the review queue, or back into the loop for a missing citation (§5.3).

Node filename == registered node name == trace span name (§9.3 rule 3).

docs.title: build_navigator_graph(settings, *, intent_chain=None, answer_writer_chain=None, explainer=None, claim_extractor_chain=None, scope_judge_chain=None, contextualizer_chain=None, checkpointer=None)
docs.text:
The only function that wires the navigator graph's nodes and edges.

The LLM-backed pieces are injectable so the graph can be assembled and tested offline with stubs; in production they are built from the configured models.

Source code in src/navigator/graph/builder.py 
def build_navigator_graph(
    settings: Settings,
    *,
    intent_chain: IntentClassifierChain | None = None,
    answer_writer_chain: AnswerWriterChain | None = None,
    explainer: Explainer | None = None,
    claim_extractor_chain: ClaimExtractorChain | None = None,
    scope_judge_chain: ScopeJudgeChain | None = None,
    contextualizer_chain: ContextualizerChain | None = None,
    checkpointer: Checkpointer = None,
) -> NavigatorGraph:
    """The only function that wires the navigator graph's nodes and edges.

    The LLM-backed pieces are injectable so the graph can be assembled and tested
    offline with stubs; in production they are built from the configured models.
    """
    record_store = RecordStore(Path(settings.record_db_path))
    education_store = EducationStore(Path(settings.education_db_path))
    policy_store = PolicyStore(Path(settings.policy_db_path))
    registry = build_registry(record_store, education_store)
    executor = ScopedToolExecutor(registry)
    rule_engine = RuleEngine(policy_store.enabled_rules())

    if (
        intent_chain is None
        or answer_writer_chain is None
        or explainer is None
        or claim_extractor_chain is None
        or scope_judge_chain is None
    ):
        fast_model = build_fast_model(settings)
        reasoning_model = build_reasoning_model(settings)
        if intent_chain is None:
            intent_chain = build_intent_classifier_chain(fast_model)
        if answer_writer_chain is None:
            answer_writer_chain = build_answer_writer_chain(reasoning_model)
        if explainer is None:
            # The explainer is bound to the full registry; the scoped executor
            # enforces the per-run ToolScope on every call, so the model can
            # propose anything and only in-scope calls execute (§3.3, §3.4).
            explainer = build_explainer(fast_model, list(registry.tools.values()))
        if claim_extractor_chain is None:
            # Claim extraction is a mechanical decomposition -> fast model.
            claim_extractor_chain = build_claim_extractor_chain(fast_model)
        if scope_judge_chain is None:
            # The scope judge is the one graded call -> reasoning model.
            scope_judge_chain = build_scope_judge_chain(reasoning_model)
        if contextualizer_chain is None:
            # Rewriting a follow-up is mechanical -> fast model. Only ever called when a
            # conversation has earlier turns.
            contextualizer_chain = build_contextualizer_chain(fast_model)

    workflow = StateGraph(NavigatorState)
    # mypy cannot resolve add_node's overloads against a factory-returned
    # Callable (vs. a plain top-level function) — confirmed upstream limitation,
    # not a real type error; each node is unit-tested directly in tests/graph/.
    workflow.add_node("intake", build_intake_node(record_store, settings))  # type: ignore[arg-type]
    # With no chain (the all-stub offline graphs) a follow-up is simply not rewritten.
    workflow.add_node("contextualize", build_contextualize_node(contextualizer_chain))  # type: ignore[arg-type]
    workflow.add_node("screen_rules", build_screen_rules_node(rule_engine))  # type: ignore[arg-type]
    workflow.add_node("classify_intent", build_classify_intent_node(intent_chain))  # type: ignore[arg-type]
    workflow.add_node("detect_language", detect_language_node)
    workflow.add_node(
        "resolve_policy",
        build_resolve_policy_node(policy_store, registry, DEFAULT_ROW_CAP),  # type: ignore[arg-type]
    )
    workflow.add_node(
        "investigate",
        build_investigate_node(  # type: ignore[arg-type]
            explainer, executor, load_prompt("explainer_v1")
        ),
    )
    workflow.add_node("draft_answer", build_draft_answer_node(answer_writer_chain))  # type: ignore[arg-type]
    workflow.add_node(
        "extract_claims",
        build_extract_claims_node(claim_extractor_chain),  # type: ignore[arg-type]
    )
    workflow.add_node(
        "post_flight",
        build_post_flight_node(  # type: ignore[arg-type]
            record_store.reference_range,
            scope_judge_chain,
            floor=settings.citation_coverage_floor,
            max_evidence_passes=settings.max_evidence_passes,
        ),
    )
    workflow.add_node("publish", build_publish_node())  # type: ignore[arg-type]
    workflow.add_node("enqueue_review", build_enqueue_review_node())  # type: ignore[arg-type]
    workflow.add_node("template_response", build_template_response_node(policy_store))  # type: ignore[arg-type]
    workflow.add_node("budget_exceeded", budget_exceeded_node)

    workflow.set_entry_point("intake")
    # screen_rules, classify_intent and detect_language run in parallel after
    # contextualize (which follows intake, §5.1); resolve_policy is their join.
    workflow.add_edge("intake", "contextualize")
    workflow.add_edge("contextualize", "screen_rules")
    workflow.add_edge("contextualize", "classify_intent")
    workflow.add_edge("contextualize", "detect_language")
    workflow.add_edge("screen_rules", "resolve_policy")
    workflow.add_edge("classify_intent", "resolve_policy")
    workflow.add_edge("detect_language", "resolve_policy")
    workflow.add_conditional_edges(
        "resolve_policy",
        route_after_resolve_policy,
        {
            "emergency": "template_response",
            "crisis": "template_response",
            "out_of_scope": "template_response",
            "clinician_review": "template_response",
            "allow": "investigate",
        },
    )
    workflow.add_conditional_edges(
        "investigate",
        route_after_investigate,
        {
            "investigate": "investigate",
            "draft_answer": "draft_answer",
            "budget_exceeded": "budget_exceeded",
        },
    )
    # Post-flight: the draft is decomposed, then the three checks run and route.
    workflow.add_edge("draft_answer", "extract_claims")
    workflow.add_edge("extract_claims", "post_flight")
    workflow.add_conditional_edges(
        "post_flight",
        route_after_post_flight,
        {
            "publish": "publish",
            "escalate": "template_response",
            "review": "enqueue_review",
            "investigate": "investigate",
        },
    )
    workflow.add_edge("publish", END)
    workflow.add_edge("enqueue_review", END)
    workflow.add_edge("template_response", END)
    workflow.add_edge("budget_exceeded", END)
    return workflow.compile(checkpointer=checkpointer)

def build_skeleton_graph() -> SkeletonGraph:
    """Phase 0 walking skeleton: echo -> done."""
    workflow = StateGraph(SkeletonState)
    workflow.add_node("echo", echo)
    workflow.add_node("done", done)
    workflow.set_entry_point("echo")
    workflow.add_edge("echo", "done")
    workflow.add_edge("done", END)
    return workflow.compile()

docs.title: Deploy to a server
docs.text:
A step-by-step guide to running Clinical Care Navigator on a Linux server behind HTTPS. It uses the repository's compose.prod.yaml, which builds the API and the web app and publishes no host ports: a reverse proxy is the only way in.

The browser talks to one origin. The proxy sends /api/* to the API (removing the /api prefix, because the API itself has no such prefix) and everything else to the web app.

How this was checked

Both images were built from the repository's Dockerfiles, started with compose.prod.yaml behind a Caddy container, and exercised in a browser: the site and /api/healthz through the proxy, a full live run with its steps streaming in as they happened, a reload replaying that run, no host ports reachable, and the basic-auth rules below. That ran on a local machine with plain HTTP, so automatic HTTPS certificates, DNS and a public firewall were not exercised; those parts rely on Caddy's documented behaviour.

docs.title: 1. What you need
docs.text:
• A Linux server with a public IP, reachable by SSH.
  • A domain name with an A record pointing at the server (for example clinical.example.com).
  • Docker Engine with the Compose plugin (docker compose version should work).
  • An OpenAI API key.
  • Ports 80 and 443 open to the internet, and nothing else except SSH.

docs.title: 2. Get the code onto the server
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/zarreh/clinical_care_navigator.git
cd clinical_care_navigator

The continuous-deployment workflow publishes the API image to GitHub Container Registry but not the web image, and its server-deploy job is still a placeholder. So this guide builds both images on the server.

docs.title: 3. Put the data on the server
docs.text:
The API reads three read-only databases from data/ (records.db, education.db, policy.db) and writes two of its own there at runtime (runs.db and checkpoints.db). data/ is git-ignored and excluded from the image, so you have to provide it. Pick one option.

Build it on the serverBuild it locally and copy it

Needs uv and outbound internet access (it downloads the public Synthea sample data and education pages).

uv sync --extra dev
make data

On the machine where you already ran make data, copy only the three read-only databases:

rsync -av \
  --include='records.db' --include='education.db' --include='policy.db' \
  --exclude='*' \
  data/ you@your-server:~/clinical_care_navigator/data/

Do not copy runs.db or checkpoints.db: they are the other machine's run history and paused reviews.

The API container runs as user 1000, so that user must be able to write to data/:

sudo chown -R 1000:1000 data

Without this the API exits at startup with sqlite3.OperationalError: unable to open database file and Application startup failed.

docs.title: 4. Configure
docs.text:
Create .env in the repository root. It is read by docker compose for the API container, and the two WEB_PUBLIC_* lines are also used as build arguments for the web image.

# --- API (runtime) ---
NAVIGATOR_OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-...
NAVIGATOR_ENVIRONMENT=production
NAVIGATOR_FRONTEND_ORIGINS='["https://clinical.example.com"]'

# --- Web (baked into the JavaScript at build time) ---
WEB_PUBLIC_API_URL=https://clinical.example.com/api
WEB_PUBLIC_DOCS_URL=https://zarreh.ai/clinical_care_navigator/
Variable Why it matters NAVIGATOR_OPENAI_API_KEY Without it, runs that need the model fail. NAVIGATOR_ENVIRONMENT Anything other than development switches logs to JSON. NAVIGATOR_FRONTEND_ORIGINS CORS allow-list as a JSON list. Outside development this is the only thing trusted (localhost is not). Because the proxy serves the site and the API from one origin the browser does not need CORS, but set it to your public origin anyway. WEB_PUBLIC_API_URL Where the browser calls the API. Must be the public URL ending in /api. The default, http://localhost/api, only works on the server itself. WEB_PUBLIC_DOCS_URL Target of every "Learn more" and Docs link. Point it at wherever you host the documentation site.

Optional: NAVIGATOR_LANGSMITH_API_KEY for tracing, NAVIGATOR_AUTONOMY_LEVEL, and the rate limits (see Run it yourself).

The two WEB_PUBLIC_* values are build-time

Next.js inlines them into the bundle. Changing them in .env does nothing until you rebuild the web image (docker compose -f compose.prod.yaml up -d --build). A site whose API calls go to localhost was built without WEB_PUBLIC_API_URL.

Keep .env out of git

It holds your API key. It is already git-ignored and excluded from the images.

docs.title: 5. Set up the reverse proxy
docs.text:
compose.prod.yaml attaches both services to an external Docker network named edge. Create it once, then run a proxy on it. These services are named navigator-api and navigator-web so they don't clash with other apps sharing the network.

docker network create edge     # skip if it already exists

Create a directory for the proxy, for example ~/proxy, with two files.

~/proxy/compose.yaml:

services:
  caddy:
    image: caddy:2
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "80:80"
      - "443:443"
    volumes:
      - ./Caddyfile:/etc/caddy/Caddyfile:ro
      - caddy_data:/data        # certificates live here
      - caddy_config:/config
    networks:
      - edge

volumes:
  caddy_data:
  caddy_config:

networks:
  edge:
    external: true

~/proxy/Caddyfile:

clinical.example.com {
    handle_path /api/* {
        reverse_proxy navigator-api:8000 {
            flush_interval -1
        }
    }

    handle {
        encode zstd gzip
        reverse_proxy navigator-web:3000
    }
}

Two details matter here:

  • handle_path strips /api before forwarding. Without it the API sees /api/conversations and returns 404.
  • flush_interval -1 sends the live run stream through immediately instead of buffering it, and encode is deliberately kept off the /api routes so the stream is never compressed into a lump.

Caddy also requests and renews the HTTPS certificate for the domain by itself.

Start it:

cd ~/proxy && docker compose up -d
Using nginx instead (not tested here)

The same four requirements apply: strip /api, do not buffer the stream, and set the client address rather than appending to what the client sent.

location /api/ {
    proxy_pass http://navigator-api:8000/;      # trailing slash strips /api
    proxy_http_version 1.1;
    proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $remote_addr;
    proxy_set_header Host $host;
    proxy_buffering off;                        # server-sent events
    proxy_read_timeout 120s;
}
location / {
    proxy_pass http://navigator-web:3000;
    proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $remote_addr;
    proxy_set_header Host $host;
}

docs.title: 6. Start the app
docs.text:
From the repository root:

docker compose -f compose.prod.yaml up -d --build

The first build takes a few minutes. The web container waits for the API's health check to pass before it starts.

Check it:

docker compose -f compose.prod.yaml ps          # both should say "healthy"
curl https://clinical.example.com/api/healthz   # {"status":"ok"}
docker compose -f compose.prod.yaml exec navigator-api printenv NAVIGATOR_FRONTEND_ORIGINS

Then open https://clinical.example.com/, run one of the example questions, and confirm the steps appear one by one and a result card shows up. A live run takes roughly 15–40 seconds.

To demonstrate the clinician review queue, which is normally empty, load three sample drafts (scripted, no model call):

docker compose -f compose.prod.yaml exec navigator-api python -m navigator.api.demo_seed

docs.title: 7. Protect the clinician review queue
docs.text:
Do this before the site is public

The app has no login. Anyone who can reach /reviews can approve, edit or decline a held answer. Putting basic auth at the proxy covers both the page and the API calls the page makes.

Generate a password hash, then add a basic_auth block to the site in your Caddyfile (above handle_path):

docker compose -f ~/proxy/compose.yaml exec caddy caddy hash-password

clinical.example.com {
    @reviews path /reviews /reviews/* /api/reviews /api/reviews/*
    basic_auth @reviews {
        clinician <paste-the-hash-here>
    }

    handle_path /api/* {
        # ...unchanged...
    }
    handle {
        # ...unchanged...
    }
}

docker compose -f ~/proxy/compose.yaml exec caddy caddy reload --config /etc/caddy/Caddyfile

With this in place the home page and /api/healthz stay public, while /reviews and every /api/reviews… request (including the decision POST) return 401 without credentials. The visitor-facing questions are unaffected. Do not try to protect the API with a key in browser code: anything in the browser is visible to everyone.

docs.title: 8. Operate it
docs.text:
Logs

docker compose -f compose.prod.yaml logs -f navigator-api

Update to a new version

git pull
docker compose -f compose.prod.yaml up -d --build

data/ is untouched. Any run in flight during the restart cannot finish; on startup the API marks it failed ("interrupted by a server restart") and puts a review that was mid-decision back in the queue, so nothing spins forever.

Back up

runs.db (conversation history and the review queue) and checkpoints.db (the paused state a held review resumes from) belong together: a review points into the checkpoint database. Back them up as a pair. The other three databases are rebuildable with make data.

mkdir -p backups
sqlite3 data/runs.db        ".backup 'backups/runs-$(date +%F).db'"
sqlite3 data/checkpoints.db ".backup 'backups/checkpoints-$(date +%F).db'"

Reset the history

Stop the stack, then delete runs.db, checkpoints.db, checkpoints.db-wal and checkpoints.db-shm together. Deleting only one leaves held reviews that can no longer be resumed.

Run one API process. Runs execute inside the API process and the stores are SQLite files, so do not scale navigator-api to several replicas or workers.

docs.title: 9. Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Likely cause and fix API container exits with unable to open database file data/ is not writable by user 1000. Run sudo chown -R 1000:1000 data. The page loads but every question fails, or the browser tries localhost WEB_PUBLIC_API_URL was missing or wrong when the web image was built. Fix .env and rebuild with up -d --build. 404 on every API call through the proxy The proxy is not stripping /api. Use handle_path (Caddy) or a trailing slash on proxy_pass (nginx). The run seems to hang, then everything appears at once The proxy is buffering the event stream. Use flush_interval -1 (Caddy) or proxy_buffering off (nginx), and do not compress /api. The page says "the API did not answer" while the API is up The browser blocked the call because the page's origin is not in NAVIGATOR_FRONTEND_ORIGINS. Add the exact public origin (scheme and host, no path) and restart the API. Everyone gets 429 Too many requests The rate limit is per client address. If the proxy does not pass the real client address, all visitors share one bucket. Make the proxy set X-Forwarded-For (Caddy does by default). Also see the limits in Run it yourself. Runs fail with an authentication error from the model NAVIGATOR_OPENAI_API_KEY is missing or wrong in .env. Recreate the container after fixing it: docker compose -f compose.prod.yaml up -d. "Docs" links go to the wrong place Set WEB_PUBLIC_DOCS_URL and rebuild the web image. The documentation site itself is published to GitHub Pages by the CD workflow; use whatever URL it ends up at.

docs.title: 10. Security notes
docs.text:
• The API trusts X-Forwarded-For from any peer (--forwarded-allow-ips "*") so the per-client rate limit sees real visitors. That is safe only because no host port is published and the proxy replaces the header; both were checked: a spoofed X-Forwarded-For sent through Caddy arrives replaced by the real address. Never publish the API port directly.
  • Open only 22, 80 and 443 in the server firewall.
  • The patient is a choice among demonstration personas, not a login: the API only answers as those personas (NAVIGATOR_DEMO_PATIENTS_ONLY, on by default), but it cannot tell who is asking. See Choose who you are asking as.
  • The data is entirely synthetic, and the app states it is not a medical device. Do not point it at real patient records: there is no setting for that and no login, audit trail or access control that real data would require.

docs.title: Regulatory basis
docs.text:
Scope of this document

This page explains the regulatory reasoning behind the system's design. It is not legal or regulatory advice, and this system is not a medical device, not a clinical decision support product, and not in clinical use.

docs.title: The design constraint that shaped the architecture
docs.text:
The 21st Century Cures Act §3060 excludes certain clinical decision support (CDS) software from the medical device definition, and the FDA's Clinical Decision Support Software guidance (September 2022) interprets it. Non-device CDS must, among other criteria, enable the user to independently review the basis for its output rather than relying primarily on it, and must not acquire, process or analyze a medical image or signal.

That criterion is why:

  • every clinical claim carries a citation, and coverage is measured and enforced in guardrails/citation_check.py rather than requested in a prompt (docs/architecture/decisions/D-A3-1-the-sandwich-has-two-independent-halves.md);
  • citations point at real public-domain pages a patient can actually open (docs/architecture/decisions/D-A3-4-citations-are-real-and-that-is-free.md) — a citation that cannot be independently reviewed satisfies nothing;
  • reference ranges are quoted rather than interpreted (store/models.py::ReferenceRange);
  • the answer shows which record rows it read (schemas/answer.py::Claim.evidence_refs);
  • the system directs to care rather than characterising urgency (guardrails/templates.py) — it never says "you are having a heart attack", it says "seek emergency care now".

Citation coverage is therefore not a quality metric here. It is a design constraint traceable to a named criterion, and being able to point at the code that enforces it is a stronger position than any amount of domain vocabulary.

docs.title: HIPAA minimum necessary — 45 CFR 164.502(b)
docs.text:
The minimum-necessary standard requires limiting use, disclosure and request of protected health information to what is reasonably necessary for the purpose. Two controls implement this directly, not as a prompt instruction:

  • Refusals short-circuit before retrieval. Any non-allow pre-flight decision binds registry.education_only_scope(), from which every patient-scoped tool is absent (tools/registry.py, docs/architecture/decisions/D-A3-6-publication-is-deterministic-and-refusals-short-circuit.md). A refused or escalated question never reaches a patient record.
  • Row caps. ScopedToolExecutor clamps every limit argument to the scope's row_cap regardless of what the model requests (tools/scoping.py), so a run cannot pull more of the record than the scope allows.

docs.title: HIPAA Safe Harbor de-identification — 45 CFR 164.514(b)
docs.text: Safe Harbor lists 18 identifier categories that must be removed for data to be considered de-identified. This system never reaches that question in the first place: every patient record is generated by Synthea (Apache-2.0), a synthetic-patient-population simulator. There is no real or re-identifiable individual behind any record this system reads, and there is no configuration path to point it at real data.

docs.title: ONC information blocking / 21st Century Cures Act Final Rule
docs.text: The Cures Act Final Rule (45 CFR Part 171) establishes that patients are entitled to their own electronic health information without unreasonable delay or interference. This is the regulatory reason a patient-facing record-access assistant exists as a category at all — the system's base tier (record lookup, lab and medication education) is squarely inside what the rule intends patients to be able to get.

docs.title: Section 1557 language access — 42 U.S.C. §18116 / 45 CFR Part 92
docs.text: The ACA §1557 language-access requirements require meaningful access for people with limited English proficiency. This is why a non-English question is not silently answered badly: canonical case 16 detects the question's language (guardrails/language.py) and responds with a stated limitation in English plus a route to the care team (guardrails/templates.py::language_limitation_template), rather than either guessing at a translation or refusing outright. base does not yet answer in Spanish; that is an honest, disclosed limitation, not a silent failure, and full language support is deferred to Stage 2 (docs/PLAN.md §7 Stretch).

docs.title: The crisis path — 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline
docs.text: A self-harm red flag routes to a dedicated crisis path (guardrails/templates.py::crisis_template), distinct from the medical emergency path in both resource and wording (docs/PLAN.md §4.4): the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline is available 24/7 by call or text, and is named explicitly rather than folded into a generic "seek care" message.

docs.title: Red-flag rules, cited rule by rule
docs.text:
Every escalation rule cites a real, public-domain patient-facing source, and the build fails if an escalation rule is added without one (data/generate_policy_rules.py::validate):

Category Rules Source Cardiac rf-cardiac-chest-pain, rf-cardiac-radiating, rf-cardiac-associated MedlinePlus — Heart Attack Stroke rf-stroke-face-arm-speech, rf-stroke-sudden-neuro MedlinePlus — Stroke Anaphylaxis rf-anaphylaxis MedlinePlus — Anaphylaxis Self-harm rf-self-harm MedlinePlus — Suicide and Suicidal Thoughts, 988

The scope rules (dosing, medication change, diagnosis requests, out-of-domain questions, interaction and symptom-management questions) carry no citation, and deliberately so: they are boundaries this project set, not clinical findings, and that distinction is worth keeping visible in the table rather than dressing a design choice up as evidence.

docs.title: Education-source terms, verified before the pipeline was written
docs.text:
The plan required these to be checked against the primary sources rather than assumed, because the whole citation argument above rests on them.

Service Terms Rate limit MedlinePlus Connect Free; no API key, no registration. Linking to and displaying returned data is permitted; copying MedlinePlus pages is not. NLM recommends caching for 12–24 hours 100 requests/minute per IP MedlinePlus Web service Free of charge; no registration or licensing 85 requests/minute per IP RxNav / RxNorm Free; no licence needed. RxClass/SNOMED CT is not used, so its Affiliate licence does not apply 20 requests/second per IP

So the education cache is a build artifact, not a corpus: it holds only the fields the service returns — title, URL, summary, attribution — with a retrieval timestamp and a TTL inside NLM's recommended window. It is never committed and the application never mirrors a MedlinePlus page. Attribution appears in NOTICE.md, including RxNav's required verbatim statement.

The LOINC terminology table is deliberately not a dependency, so its licence agreement never applies. Synthea's observations already carry LOINC codes and MedlinePlus Connect accepts a code directly; codes pass through, the table is never downloaded or redistributed.

docs.title: Two disclosures made deliberately
docs.text:
No clinician has reviewed the safety rules. Every emergency red-flag rule is derived from a published patient-facing source and cites it by URL, so no rule rests on the author's own clinical judgement. But no clinician reviewed the resulting table. Stating that plainly is the honest position; an uncited table reviewed informally would be worse than a cited one reviewed by nobody.

The reference ranges are illustrative. data/lab_reference_ranges.csv is adult-general and cited to published sources. It is not any laboratory's own reference intervals, and real ranges vary by assay, method, age and sex.

docs.title: Run it yourself
docs.text: Everything here runs from a clean clone. No account, no course data, and no real patient data is involved at any point.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Python 3.12+
  • uv
  • Docker (optional, for make up)
  • An OpenAI API key, for the phases that make model calls

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
git clone <repo>
cd clinical_care_navigator
uv sync --extra dev
cp .env.example .env       # add NAVIGATOR_OPENAI_API_KEY

docs.title: Build the data
docs.text:
make data

This generates the synthetic Synthea population, builds the record store, renders the clinical notes, fetches the public-domain education content, and generates the safety policy tables. It writes nothing outside data/, and data/ is gitignored.

The build fails loudly rather than coercing: an education row with an unresolvable citation, or a reference-range row with no cited source, stops the build.

docs.title: Run
docs.text:
make run          # API on :8000 and the frontend on :3000 together
make dev          # API only, http://localhost:8000  (docs at /docs)
make up           # the API in Docker

Nothing calls the model until you ask: the homepage explains the app and offers four example questions plus a free-text box. A live run takes roughly 15–40 seconds; questions stopped at pre-flight finish in a second or two. Each run gets its own URL (/?run=<id>), so a refresh or a shared link replays it from the store.

If the API restarts while a run is in flight, that run can never finish. On startup the API marks such runs failed ("interrupted by a server restart") and returns any review left mid-decision to pending, so the UI shows an error instead of spinning. This assumes one API process owns the run store; do not run several workers against the same runs.db.

docs.title: Choose who you are asking as
docs.text:
The app has no sign-in, so the homepage asks "Who are you asking as?" and offers a handful of synthetic patients. They are picked at runtime from the record store by what each record can show off, ranked by how much history it has, so they stay correct when the data is rebuilt:

Persona Chosen as Good for A full record The richest history in the data Asking about labs, medications and conditions A hidden critical value The patient the build planted a critical potassium on The safety override Basic health literacy The richest other basic-literacy patient with an A1c The easier reading target (grade 6) and its measured grade Spanish-speaking patient The richest Spanish-language patient with an A1c The stated-limitation reply A visit note with a planted instruction The patient the build planted an injected note on Showing a note is treated as data, not obeyed

The two patients tied to planted data are whoever the data build planted the fact on, so their histories are not chosen for size; the cards show each record's size so you can see that. A role the data cannot fill is skipped, and a small store is topped up with its richest patients, so the list is never empty.

The choice lives in the URL (?patient=…), so a shared link keeps who it was asked as, and every run and every held review shows its patient. The four example questions ask as the persona whose record they need.

A demo selector, not authentication

Choosing a patient on the page is not the same as being that patient. The API only answers as these personas (NAVIGATOR_DEMO_PATIENTS_ONLY), which keeps a caller from reading arbitrary records, but it does not know who you are. Real use needs sign-in: the server would learn the patient from the session instead of from the request, and GET /personas and the picker would go away.

docs.title: Follow-up questions
docs.text:
An answer is not the end of the conversation. Under a finished answer there is an Ask a follow-up box, so you can say "what about the one before that?" or "is that normal?" and be understood. The earlier questions fold away above, each with its status, and Start a new conversation begins again.

How it works, and why it is still safe:

  • A follow-up is an ordinary run. It goes through the same graph, the same pre-flight gate, scoped tools and post-flight checks as any question. Nothing is skipped because it is "only" a follow-up, and a held draft goes to the clinician queue as usual.
  • One extra step, only when needed. A new first step, contextualize, rewrites a message that depends on the earlier turns into a standalone question ("Is that one normal?" becomes "Is my A1c result of 2.4% on August 5, 2026, normal?"). A first question has no history, so it skips this step and costs nothing extra. The rewrite is shown in the run ("Understood as…") so you can see how you were understood.
  • A rewrite cannot lower the safety decision. The deterministic red-flag screen reads both your own words and the rewrite, the classifier is shown both, and language is detected on what you typed. A symptom mentioned inside a follow-up still reaches emergency guidance. If the rewrite fails, the run carries on with exactly what you typed.
  • The patient never changes mid-conversation. A follow-up stays with the patient the conversation began with; ask as someone else by starting a new conversation.
  • Only the latest answer can be followed up, and only once it has finished, so a thread cannot fork. Answers held for a clinician are noted to the rewriter as "held", never quoted.
  • Conversations are capped (NAVIGATOR_MAX_CONVERSATION_TURNS, default 8) and the rewriter sees only the most recent turns (NAVIGATOR_CONVERSATION_CONTEXT_TURNS, default 3), which bounds cost.

Behind the scenes a conversation is a chain of runs (conversation_id and turn on each), and GET /conversations/{id}/thread lists a conversation's turns. Databases created before follow-ups existed are upgraded in place on the next start.

docs.title: Demo the clinician review queue
docs.text:
Held answers only appear when post-flight refuses to publish a draft, which a well-behaved model rarely produces, so the queue is usually empty. To demonstrate the clinician's part, load four sample items:

make seed-reviews

Refresh /reviews and you will find four drafts, each held for a different reason: one tells the patient what to do about their treatment, one contradicts the patient's actual A1c, one makes a clinical claim with no evidence behind it, and one is a safe "I don't have that, ask your care team" reply to a general question ("What is the bad cholesterol?") that post-flight held because its only claim had nothing to cite. Approve, edit or decline each: a decision really resumes the paused run, and you can open "See how this draft was produced" to follow it.

The drafts are scripted, not model output (it needs no API key and costs nothing), but they run through the real graph, the real post-flight checks and the real checkpoint store, and the text is built from the patient's real A1c result. Running it twice is safe (cases already seeded are skipped); add --again to create fresh copies after you have decided the first set:

uv run python -m navigator.api.demo_seed --again

On a deployed server, run it inside the API container:

docker compose -f compose.prod.yaml exec navigator-api python -m navigator.api.demo_seed

docs.title: Inspect the graph in LangGraph Studio
docs.text:
uv sync --extra dev   # installs the langgraph CLI
make studio           # local server on http://127.0.0.1:2024

make studio starts langgraph dev on the real navigator graph (the same construction the API uses, from src/navigator/studio.py, registered in langgraph.json). Open the Studio URL it prints (https://smith.langchain.com/studio/?baseUrl=http://127.0.0.1:2024), pick the navigator graph, and you can see all thirteen nodes, step through a run, inspect the state after each node, and edit state and replay.

Studio starts a run from a state, not a question. Give it these three fields:

{
  "question": "What is an A1c test?",
  "patient_id": "<a patient id from your record store>",
  "run_id": "studio-1"
}

Get a patient id with:

uv run python -c "from pathlib import Path; from navigator.store import RecordStore; print(RecordStore(Path('data/records.db')).patient_ids()[0])"

Things to know:

  • It needs the data built (make data) and NAVIGATOR_OPENAI_API_KEY in .env, because it runs the real model.
  • Studio supplies its own in-memory persistence, so the enqueue_review interrupt pauses and resumes inside Studio (resume with {"action": "approve"}), but nothing is written to runs.db or the review queue, and nothing shows up in the web app.
  • The local server needs no key. The Studio page itself is hosted by LangChain and asks you to sign in to LangSmith in the browser.
  • It is a development tool. Do not run it on a server.

docs.title: Check
docs.text:
make check        # ruff, mypy --strict, import-linter, pytest
make eval         # layer 1 canonical regression set
make docs         # this site, locally

There is no setting that points this application at a real record system.

docs.title: Deploy
docs.text:
See Deploy to a server for the full walkthrough: server and DNS prerequisites, getting the data onto the machine, .env, the reverse proxy, protecting the clinician review queue, updating, backups and troubleshooting.

The two points that bite most often:

  • WEB_PUBLIC_API_URL and WEB_PUBLIC_DOCS_URL are baked into the web image at build time; changing them requires docker compose -f compose.prod.yaml up -d --build.
  • There is no login. Put basic auth at the proxy in front of /reviews and /api/reviews, or anyone can decide a held answer.

docs.title: Data pipeline
docs.text:
In one paragraph, for a non-engineer

Nothing here is a real patient. The records are generated by an open-source simulator, and the health information the assistant cites comes from public, government-run pages that anyone can open. Both are rebuilt from scratch by one command; neither is stored in this repository.

docs.title: Four sources
docs.text: Need Source Licence In the repo? Patient records Synthea Apache-2.0 No — generated by make data Lab reference ranges data/lab_reference_ranges.csv Original work, each row cited Yes, small Education content MedlinePlus + RxNav/RxNorm (NLM) US Government work, public domain. Free, no key, no registration No — fetched at build time Safety policy rules generate_policy_rules.py Original work, red flags cited Generated

docs.title: Why the citations are real
docs.text:
Generating education text with a language model and attaching a citation_url to it would produce an app whose citations point at sources that did not say the thing being cited — in an app whose entire argument is that every claim carries a citation. That is a category error, not a shortcut.

MedlinePlus Connect resolves a LOINC code to the matching lab-test page and an RxCUI to the matching drug page. The LOINC table is deliberately not a dependency: Synthea's observations already carry the code, so the licensed terminology download never enters the pipeline.

Where no vetted page exists, the assistant says so. It does not substitute a similar test and it does not generate content. In a citation-grounded system a visible coverage gap is a feature.

docs.title: Two gaps Synthea has, and how they are filled
docs.text: Gap Fix No free-text clinical notes render_notes.py composes them deterministically from the structured record using templates. Stated plainly as rendered, not authored No reference ranges or flags lab_reference_ranges.csv — small, hand-curated, LOINC-keyed, three bands per analyte, every row citing its published source

docs.title: Build
docs.text:
make data

Five steps, in order: fetch the population, build the typed store, render notes, fetch education, generate the rule table, bind the scenarios.

The build fails loudly rather than degrading:

Condition Result A reference band with no cited source or no verbatim quote Build fails A critical band asserted without a citation Build fails — leave it empty instead An escalation rule with no published source URL and quote Build fails An emitted citation URL that does not resolve Build fails More or fewer than one planted injection fixture Build fails

It never coerces a bad value into a plausible one.

docs.title: What the build produced
docs.text:
Measure Value Patients 25, selected deterministically toward covered analytes Rendered notes 150, byte-stable for a fixed store Reference-range rows 27, every band quoted from its published source Rows with a cited critical band 8 Safety rules 14, every escalation rule citing and quoting a source Education pages 321 across 149 distinct URLs, all verified reachable Declared coverage gaps 18

See the data profile for the coverage chart.

docs.title: Two honesty notes
docs.text:
Reference ranges are quoted, not paraphrased. Each row carries the sentence its band came from, so an answer can show a reader the published text rather than asking them to trust a number. Where no published threshold could be quoted — a critical high for sodium, a critical low for calcium — the band is left empty rather than estimated.

The education cache is a build artifact, not a corpus. NLM permits linking to and displaying what its services return, and recommends caching for 12–24 hours; it does not permit copying MedlinePlus pages. So the cache holds only returned fields with a retrieval timestamp, it is never committed, and the committed test fixture carries citation metadata with the page bodies stripped.

docs.title: Architecture overview
docs.text:
In one paragraph, for a non-engineer

The system is a small state machine. Each box does one job and hands its result to the next. Two of the boxes are safety checks — one before the assistant reads anything, one after it has written a draft — and the boxes that make the final decisions are ordinary code, not the language model.

docs.title: Five properties this is designed to have
docs.text:
1. Both halves of the sandwich assess independently. Pre-flight judges the question; post-flight judges the evidence and the answer.
  2. Refusal short-circuits before any patient data is read. Minimum necessary is enforced by topology, not by filtering afterwards.
  3. One model call before any evidence is gathered. screen_rules and resolve_policy are code. Don't spend a model call on a decision an if can make. (A follow-up question adds one cheap call first, contextualize, to make it stand on its own; a first question never pays for it. See Follow-up questions.)
  4. Cheap checks run before expensive ones. Critical-value and citation checks are pure code and can short-circuit the judge.
  5. Publication is deterministic. publish emits the already-judged draft; it contains no model call and cannot alter the text.

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
• The node filename equals the registered node name equals the trace span name.
  • builder.py is the only file that wires nodes and edges, so the whole control flow reads in one screen.
  • Nodes orchestrate, chains compute, agents decide. Each node receives a narrow read-only projection of state, not the whole blob.
  • Prompts are versioned files referenced by id, never string literals in logic.

Layering is enforced in CI by import-linter: api → graph → guardrails → tools → retrieval → store → schemas.

docs.title: The policy engine
docs.text:
In one paragraph, for a non-engineer

Before the assistant looks at anything, the question passes two checks that run at the same time: a fast list-based one and a slower language-model one. A piece of ordinary code combines their verdicts, always taking the more cautious of the two, and records when they disagreed.

Arrives in Phase 3.

docs.title: Why not just match keywords
docs.text:
The obvious approach — check whether a red-flag phrase appears in the text — fails in both directions, and both failures are one line long:

Input Keyword matching Correct "I feel like an elephant is sitting on my chest" no match → answer emergency "my discharge note says to watch for chest pain" match → emergency ordinary answer "is it okay to come off my metformin" no match → answer out of scope

Over-refusal is the failure mode that gets safety systems switched off, and it is the one nobody measures.

docs.title: The three layers
docs.text:
Layer Kind Catches Misses screen_rules Compiled patterns, word-boundary aware, with a negation and attribution check Explicit red-flag and dosing language. Fast, free, fully auditable Paraphrase, metaphor, other languages classify_intent One structured model call Metaphor, paraphrase, indirect phrasing Adversarial phrasing aimed at it resolve_policy Code Combines by fixed severity precedence, applies the autonomy boundary, selects the tool scope —

The negation and attribution check is what makes the second row of the table above work: a red-flag term quoted from the patient's own record, or under a negation, is attributed rather than asserted.

Precedence is fixed: direct_to_emergency_care > crisis > out_of_scope > clinician_review > allow. Where the layers disagree the more restrictive wins, and the disagreement is recorded — the disagreement rate is itself a published number.

docs.title: Post-flight
docs.text:
In one paragraph, for a non-engineer

After the assistant writes a draft, three checks run on it: does anything it found in the record demand escalation regardless of the question; does every clinical statement have a source you can open; and does the draft do any of four things it is never allowed to do. Only the last one uses a language model, and it is only reached if the first two pass.

docs.title: 1 · critical_value — pure code
docs.text:
Every lab value the run retrieved is compared against data/lab_reference_ranges.csv. A value in a critical band forces escalation per the rule table, regardless of what the question was or what the draft said. It cites the range row, so the basis is visible.

This is the check that makes "what does my potassium of 6.9 mean?" work.

docs.title: 2 · citation_coverage — pure code
docs.text:
Claims are classified as clinical or navigational. Every clinical claim must carry at least one evidence reference resolving to a recorded tool call or an education-source URL. Navigational claims ("you can message your care team") are exempt, explicitly.

Below the floor, the run returns to investigate once, with the specific uncited claims as feedback — not a generic retry.

docs.title: 3 · scope_judge — one model call
docs.text:
Four closed questions, each with a span:

  • Does the draft diagnose?
  • Does it recommend a medication or dose change?
  • Does it direct clinical action beyond contacting a clinician?
  • Does it contradict the retrieved record?

Four booleans with spans are testable. "Is this safe?" is not — a broad safety judgement from a model is unmeasurable and unfalsifiable, and each of these four maps to a specific rule a clinical owner can point at.

docs.title: Authority
docs.text: Post-flight may escalate a run that pre-flight allowed. It may never relax a pre-flight restriction. Asserted by test.

docs.title: State and flow
docs.text:
In one paragraph, for a non-engineer

Each step of the system can only see the information it needs. The step that classifies your question, for example, never sees any of your clinical data at all.

The real state model arrives in Phase 3; Phase 0 ships only a walking-skeleton state that exists to prove the streaming path.

docs.title: Narrow projections
docs.text:
Every node receives a read-only projection of state rather than the whole blob.

Node Sees classify_intent The question and the patient's literacy level. No clinical content investigate The policy decision, the tool scope, evidence gathered so far extract_claims The draft answer only post_flight Draft, evidence records, pre-flight decision. Not the raw message history publish The judged answer and the policy record

classify_intent not seeing clinical content is a deliberate privacy property, not an optimisation.

docs.title: Bounded loops
docs.text:
Both counted in state, both with a test asserting termination:

  • evidence_pass ≤ 1 — one repair pass for uncited claims
  • tool_calls ≤ max_tool_calls — plus a token and wall-clock ceiling

On breach the run terminates with a conservative templated response and the reason recorded. It never silently truncates a clinical answer.

docs.title: Streaming
docs.text:
The API bridges astream_events to Server-Sent Events, one event per node. The node filter is name == metadata["langgraph_node"], because conditional-edge routing functions also emit on_chain_end carrying the source node in their metadata under their own function name.

Graph state.

SkeletonState is the Phase 0 walking skeleton, kept so the streaming path stays proven end to end. NavigatorState is the real state (docs/PLAN.md §5.1), carrying the pre-flight decision, the scoped-executor output, and the draft.

The narrow per-node projections (§5.4) are enforced by what each node reads, not by separate TypedDicts: classify_intent reads only the question and the patient's literacy level — never clinical content — which is a deliberate, defensible privacy property stated in the docs.

docs.title: NavigatorState
docs.text:
Bases: TypedDict

The real graph state (§5.1).

total=False because the state accumulates: intake sets the patient header, the pre-flight gate sets the decision, investigate appends evidence, and draft_answer sets the draft. Keys are present only after the node that owns them has run.

Source code in src/navigator/graph/state.py 
class NavigatorState(TypedDict, total=False):
    """The real graph state (§5.1).

    `total=False` because the state accumulates: intake sets the patient header,
    the pre-flight gate sets the decision, investigate appends evidence, and
    draft_answer sets the draft. Keys are present only after the node that owns
    them has run.
    """

    # intake
    question: str
    # Earlier turns of this conversation, oldest first, each {"question", "answer"}.
    history: list[dict[str, str]]
    # contextualize: set only when a follow-up was rewritten. `question` then holds the
    # standalone rewrite and this holds the patient's own words.
    original_question: str
    patient_id: str
    run_id: str
    literacy_level: str
    language: str
    autonomy_level: str
    started_at: float

    # pre-flight gate
    rule_matches: list[RuleMatch]
    intent: IntentAssessment
    question_language: str
    policy_decision: PolicyDecision

    # investigate (the scoped executor's output)
    messages: list[BaseMessage]
    evidence: list[EvidenceRecord]
    security_events: list[SecurityEvent]
    tool_call_count: int

    # draft
    draft: PatientAnswer

    # post-flight (the centrepiece — §5.3)
    claims: list[Claim]
    evidence_pass: int
    post_flight: PostFlightResult
    published: PatientAnswer

docs.text:
